summary.headline: RMC Switchgears FY26 consolidated revenue rose 26.4% to Rs 401.59 crore, but profit fell short, with Q4 back to Rs 9.3 crore net profit after a Q3 loss of Rs 7.07 crore.
summary.overview: Management framed the call as an analyst day rather than a results discussion, covering FY26 as a year of progress and learning. Consolidated revenue grew 26.4% to Rs 401.59 crore, but margins were hit by PulseBox product development spend, rain-delayed execution in Maharashtra, and solar EPC cost pressure from China-linked supply, safeguard duty and aluminium/silver prices. Q4 returned to profit (Rs 9.3 crore) from a Rs 7.07 crore loss in Q3, which management attributed to execution catch-up and better material availability. Receivables rose from Rs 148 crore to Rs 205 crore and operating cash flow turned negative; management attributed this mainly to March-concentrated billing. No FY27 revenue or profit guidance was given; management said the unexecuted order book is about Rs 850 crore plus and the tender pipeline about Rs 1,500 crore plus.

financial_highlights.change: Up from Rs 148 crore in prior year
Management estimate, exact figures to be sent

segments.name: Electrical products
segments.commentary: About 30% of electrical product revenue is government and about 70% B2B, per management. Overall company revenue is stated as roughly 95% government and 5% B2B.

segments.name: Solar EPC
segments.commentary: Management said it converted the maximum solar EPC sales this year. Older orders were cancelled, reworked or deferred due to input cost moves, and some procurement cycles extended by nearly 2 months.

segments.name: Electrical EPC
segments.commentary: Government-linked. Management cited electrical EPC cycles of about 2 years. No revenue split disclosed.

segments.name: PulseBox (IoT distribution monitoring)
segments.commentary: Pre-revenue. POC completed; one utility has moved to formal specification and tender-document stage. Management claims it is the only player in this niche. Addressable market estimated at Rs 50,000 crore plus, not guidance.

guidance_outlook: No FY27 revenue or profit guidance given; management said it is too early in the year.
Management expects FY27 to be better than FY26 and says more buffer will be built into project timelines.
Management expects positive operating cash flow in FY27, with H1 FY27 expected to bring most retention money (typically 10% of project value, paid after completion).
Long-term aspiration of Rs 5,000 crore revenue by FY30 reiterated as intact; management also referenced 10x growth from the current base.
Strategy shifts to selecting projects on bottom line and cash flow rather than top line.
capex_capacity: No capacity, utilisation or capex figures were disclosed on the call.
PulseBox R&D is ongoing; management said the R&D team has moved to a different project and declined to give details.
Management said adding B2B / medium- and high-voltage products is at feasibility study stage and is mainly a human-resource capability build, not capex-led.
demand_pricing: Management cited government plans for about Rs 9 lakh crore of transmission investment to 2032, RDSS phase two, and a 102 GW floating solar requirement as demand drivers.
Input cost pressure from aluminium, silver, steel, copper, polymers and plastics; WPI inflation was 3.88% in March 2026.
Management described the EPC business as operating in a 'red ocean' where price decides outcomes, and positioned PulseBox as a differentiated, technology-led offering.
Management said PulseBox is 15-20% pricier than traditional distribution boxes, per its unit economics.

qa_highlights.question: What is the unexecuted order book and tender pipeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Unexecuted order book is about Rs 850 crore plus across all segments; tender pipeline is about Rs 1,500 crore plus.

qa_highlights.question: Why did receivables rise and operating cash flow turn negative?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said most supply billing happened in March because of H2 delays, and payment follows installation, so the cash lands in the next year. Only 3% to 5% of receivables, excluding retention, is above 6 months, per management. Exact figures to follow by email.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 guidance and order book execution timing?
qa_highlights.answer: No guidance given. Management said electrical EPC takes about 2 years, solar about 1 year and products about 3 months, and that buffers will be added. Order book breakdown by solar and products to be emailed.

qa_highlights.question: What is the B2B vs B2G split and target mix?
qa_highlights.answer: About 5% B2B and 95% B2G on a total basis. Management wants more B2B to reduce debtor days, but said government will stay the larger share.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Rs 5,000 crore FY30 aspiration still intact?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the aspiration remains intact, citing growth from Rs 40 crore to Rs 410 crore over four years and the ability to bid larger tenders.

qa_highlights.question: What is the PulseBox commercial status and competition?
qa_highlights.answer: One utility is in specification and tender-document discussions after a 7-day POC that generated about 388 alarms, leading to a transformer replacement. Management said RMC is currently the only player in this gap.

risks_watch: Negative operating cash flow and receivables at Rs 205 crore; watch collections and retention release in H1 FY27.
Margin pressure from solar input costs (aluminium, silver, module costs) and wider commodity inflation.
Execution delays, order cancellations and re-work in solar EPC; procurement cycles extended by nearly 2 months.
PulseBox commercial conversion depends on utility approvals, tendering and pricing; still pre-revenue.
Management declined to share details of a 'strategic collaboration' or the technology partner, citing trade secrets.
Management declined to comment on the share price fall of over 75% from its peak.
Management said it will email the order book breakdown and receivables aging details, which were not provided on the call.
summary.management_tone: Confident on long-term aspiration and PulseBox, but cautious and somewhat evasive on near-term numbers: no FY27 guidance, deferred breakdowns to email, and declined several questions on collaboration, R&D and stock price.
key_quotes: We would request investors not to view Q3 as a standalone quarter.
Our objective is not growth at any cost. Rather, our objective is profitable, sustainable, and high-quality growth.
This is not guidance. It is not an order book. It is not a revenue forecast, it is a way to understand the size of the problem that PulseBox is designed to address.
I can send you, sir, please email me this question, because right now I don't have it, I will send you.

growth.why: No FY27 revenue or profit guidance was given; management only said FY27 should be better than FY26, backed by an unexecuted order book of about Rs 850 crore plus and a Rs 1,500 crore plus tender pipeline, with no capacity additions or capex disclosed.
